data.gender_notes: Fara is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Persian origin, Fara means 'Exalted One'. This name is often given to girls in Iran and other Middle Eastern countries. It is a name with rich history and cultural significance, rooted in the ancient Persian civilization. The name Fara carries the meaning “Exalted One” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Fara usually hope their child will grow to embody exalted one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of exalted spiritual status and divine grace.
data.etymology: Fara belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Exalted One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fara total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: פארה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פארה נגזר מהמילה העברית 'פרה', שפירושה פנים או מראה. הוא קשור לנושא של הופעה אלוהית או התגלות אלוקית. השם משמש לעיתים קרובות בהקשרים של פנים אלוהיים או ה' אלוקים.

in_greek.name: Φαρά
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Φαρά συνδέεται με την έννοια του φωτός και της εκδήλωσης του Θεού. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα αυτό μπορεί να σχετίζεται με την έννοια της φανέρωσης ή της εμφάνισης του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Fara
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Fara derivatur ex hebraico 'parah', quod faciem vel aspectum significat. In traditione christiana, nomen Fara potest referri ad faciem Dei vel ad manifestationem divinam.

in_english.name: Fara
in_english.meaning: Face of God or Divine Manifestation
in_english.long_meaning: The name Fara originates from the Hebrew word 'parah', meaning face or appearance. It is associated with the concept of divine manifestation or the face of God. In Christian tradition, Fara symbolizes spiritual insight and connection with the divine. Historically, the name reflects the biblical theme of encountering God's presence.
